Implemented as change https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1673 (commit 2e3d3d4e51, stacked on 1669/1662).

PREMISE VERIFIED in origin/main cc69cc1179. close_ticket commits the STATUS event and releases the lock BEFORE the signing tail; the SigningError catch wrote a warning to stderr and fell through to the normal success payload, which carried no field about the signature outcome. Confirmed: exit 0, ticket closed-without-signature, loss undetectable programmatically.

CHANGE. completion_signature {signed, cause, error} on every close where a signature was in play. Closed vocabulary: signed / sign_failed / material_drifted / force_bypassed. Absent for a plain transition and for idea -> closed (transition_close.py excludes that edge from the signing block entirely — a REJECT/DROP is not a completion, so inventing a cause would misreport a deliberate non-event). Threaded through _lib_writes.transition, the CLI --output json branch, the TransitionResult TypedDict and transition_result.schema.json; MCP inherits from the library and is asserted, not assumed.

MESSAGE. Now leads with '<id> IS CLOSED — the close committed. Only the completion signature failed' and tells the reader NOT to re-run the transition. The old text appended the raw signing error, so a lock timeout read as a failed close.

EXIT CODE DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED, and this narrows the ticket's original AC1. docs/exit-codes.md declares the contract frozen as of the 2026-06-09 window, pinned by tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_exit_codes.py, with the table at :158 fixing transition at 0/1/10. A new code is additive-only in a future window (a release decision). Reusing exit 1 would be actively harmful: agents read 1 as 'the transition failed' and re-run it, which then exits 10 (already closed) — trading a silent loss for a louder wrong answer. The report explicitly sanctioned 'at minimum a machine-readable failure marker', which is what shipped. A test pins exit 0 so the decision is not silently reversed.

SPLIT OUT. The original AC 'detectable by a later reader' is NOT delivered here. The first draft proposed a best-effort audit comment; plan review correctly blocked it, because that comment appends through the SAME event_append -> write_lock path whose 60s timeout causes the bug, so it would be missing in exactly the case it exists for. The sound mechanism records the expectation in the same locked write as the STATUS event — an event-schema change — tracked as mechanical-coherent-wolverine (23b2-1a94-6a01-466b), linked discovered_from this ticket.

COMPLEXITY RATCHET. The added branches pushed close_ticket past its recorded ceiling (scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py, increased=1). Rather than raise the ceiling on a shrink-only gate, extracted the signing tail to _sign_completion_and_report — drift refusal vs sign vs sign failure is a decision of its own. Gate now increased=0, stale=1.

EVIDENCE. 11 tests in tests/unit/test_transition_close.py + 2 MCP facade tests in tests/interfaces/facades/test_transition_completion_signature_facade.py (13 passed). Wider -k 'transition or close or lock or schema': 1035 passed, 4 skipped. make lint (incl. complexity baseline) and make typecheck (510 files) clean.
